title: Best compact SUV in this price range
reviewText: I've been driving the Kia Sonet for over a year now and it has been an absolute joy. The build quality is impressive, the features list is extensive, and the driving dynamics are sorted. The diesel engine is refined and the iMT gearbox is a unique offering. Highly recommended for city and highway driving.
cons: Rear seat space could be better

title: Good value but some niggles
reviewText: The Sonet delivers a premium experience at a competitive price. The infotainment system is top-notch and the connected car features work well. However, I've noticed some rattling from the dashboard after 8000 km. Service experience has been average so far.

title: Stylish and feature-rich
reviewText: Bought the HTX variant and it offers great value. The styling turns heads everywhere I go. The 1.5L diesel is peppy enough for overtakes and cruises effortlessly on highways. Air purifier and sunroof are great additions at this price point.

title: Luxury redefined in India
reviewText: The Audi Q7 is a masterpiece of engineering. The virtual cockpit, the quattro system, the air suspension — everything works in perfect harmony. Yes, it's expensive to maintain, but if you can afford the car, the running costs are justified. The 3.0 TDI is silky smooth.

title: Great highway cruiser
reviewText: We use the Q7 primarily for long road trips and it excels there. The ride quality is phenomenal, the 7-seater configuration is practical, and the Bose sound system is concert-quality. City driving is the only weak point due to its sheer size.

title: Underrated sedan
reviewText: The Skoda Slavia is genuinely underrated. The 1.5 TSI engine is an absolute gem — punchy, refined, and fuel-efficient for a turbo petrol. The handling is European and the build quality is reassuring. Just wish the after-sales network was better outside metros.

title: The ultimate driving machine lives up to its name
reviewText: Upgraded from a Creta to the BMW X1 and the difference is night and day. The driving dynamics, the cabin quality, the badge value — everything is a massive step up. The 2.0L diesel is powerful yet efficient. BMW service packages make ownership hassle-free.

title: Nothing comes close at this price
reviewText: The Lexus RX is peak reliability meets luxury. Toyota's legendary quality with Lexus refinement. The hybrid powertrain is smooth and surprisingly efficient. The cabin is whisper-quiet and the Mark Levinson audio system is worth every rupee.

title: Best in segment safety
reviewText: Bought the Nexon primarily for its 5-star safety rating and it hasn't disappointed. The turbo petrol is punchy, the cabin is well-equipped, and the ride quality is plush. Tata's build quality has improved dramatically. The touchscreen could be more responsive though.

title: Perfect city SUV
reviewText: The Nexon is perfect for Bangalore traffic. Compact enough to maneuver, high enough to handle speed bumps, and loaded with features. The AMT works well in stop-and-go traffic. After 15 months, zero issues. Tata has really stepped up their game.

title: Great city hatchback
reviewText: The Grand i10 Nios is the perfect first car. Refinement levels are class-leading, the cabin feels premium for the price, and Hyundai's aftersales is excellent. The 1.2 petrol is adequate and returns good mileage. Only miss a sunroof at this price.
cons: Rear AC vents missing in base

title: The enthusiast's hatchback
reviewText: The Swift continues to be the benchmark hot hatch in India. Light steering, peppy engine, and fun to drive character make it special. The new Z-series engine is more efficient too. Interior quality has improved but still falls behind Hyundai/Tata.

title: The complete sedan package
reviewText: Honda City has been our family car for generations. This 5th gen continues the legacy. The 1.5 i-VTEC is bulletproof, the ride quality is plush, and the cabin is airy. Lane Watch camera is a thoughtful feature. Honda's reliability is unmatched in this segment.

title: Feature king of SUVs
reviewText: The Seltos set the benchmark for features in the mid-size SUV segment and continues to hold that crown. The 1.5 turbo petrol DCT is the sweet spot — fast, efficient, and smooth. The ADAS suite works reliably on highways. Excellent highway manners overall.

title: Road presence of a Range Rover
reviewText: The Harrier commands attention on the road like no other Indian SUV. The 2.0 Kryotec diesel is torquey and the 6-speed AT shifts well. The ride quality on the ALFA platform is sorted. Wish the petrol option was available. Interior quality has massive improvements over the previous gen.
